summary.text: This opportunity briefing explores combining pruning, quantization, and token reduction to address the high computational demands, large parameter footprints, and memory bandwidth bottlenecks of deep neural networks and large multimodal models. By uniting these methods, the system jointly minimizes sequence length, network parameters, and storage precision for efficient model deployment. Evidence shows that these approaches are complementary and can be integrated into open-source architectures to support resource-constrained deployments.

target_user.text: Machine learning engineers and developers deploying large language models, vision-language models, and convolutional networks on resource-constrained edge devices or cloud infrastructure.

jtbd.text: Optimize resource-constrained neural network and multimodal models for efficient inference by simultaneously reducing token counts, pruning redundant structures, and quantizing weights and activations.

value_prop.text: Provides a comprehensive compression pipeline that lowers memory footprint, decreases sequence length overhead, and improves inference throughput without requiring extensive retraining.

riskiest_assumption.text: Combining token reduction, pruning, and low-bit quantization simultaneously will introduce severe compounded accuracy degradation or instability due to conflicting approximation errors across different model components (feasibility score 2.0 out of 5.0).

mvp.text: Build a technical proof of concept script using existing packages to apply token reduction, structured pruning, and quantization to a baseline vision-language model, measuring accuracy and latency changes (proposed threshold: maximum 5 percent accuracy drop).
mvp.type: technical proof of concept from existing packages

success_metric.text: Achieve at least a proposed threshold of 2.0x end-to-end inference speedup while maintaining a proposed threshold of 95 percent or higher of the baseline task accuracy across validation benchmarks.

kill_criteria.text: The combined pipeline causes an accuracy drop exceeding a proposed threshold of 15 percent on core benchmarks, or induces unrecoverable catastrophic generation loops.
